description: The short Heritage escape spelling `op`, EXECUTED at the top level, carries the same CANONICAL `params.keyword` `"return"` as `output` and as Core `return` (issue #741) — `code`, `params`, `stage` and `severity` byte-identical to the Core twin `tests/conformance/core-language/execution/procedure-return-outside-proc`, and to the sibling `heritage/execution/heritage-output-canonical-keyword-executed-outside-proc`. Both Heritage spellings are fixtured because a param that varies with the spelling varies per spelling: `op` is a separate surface word reaching the same `params`, and asserting only `output` would leave the value `op` produces unpinned. `source_span` covers the whole `op 5` statement (4 columns against the 8 of `output 5`), so a shorter spelling still spans what the learner wrote — canonicalizing the param did not canonicalize the span. The prose still says `op`, which the localization boundary `spec/error-model.md:254-259` permits.

diagnostics.message: op only reports a value from inside a procedure. put it between 'define' and 'end'.
